ThermoPheno 0.2.0 – update report

Source: UPDATE_REPORT_ThermoPheno_v0.2.0.md

Prepared 22 November 2026. Covers the calibration/simulation thermal-time mismatch, the fix, the rerun of the DWD validation and its comparison with 0.1.1. Every number below comes from a run whose script and log are in the repository (paths given). Status: the work is in the working tree of main, not committed, not pushed, no pull request and no release yet (see section 7).

1. Diagnosis

Script: validation/diagnose_tt_consistency.R (calibration harvest years 1991–2010 only; it re-uses the input/parsing code of the validation script unchanged and the same station-selection rule). Run against the installed v0.1.1 tag. Log and tables: validation/diagnostics/v0.1.1/.

Fidelity check: the diagnostic reproduces the published 0.1.1 calibration exactly (60/60 station requirements and 952 seasonal sums identical, maximum difference 0).

  1. = raw triangular sum over the observed sowing–harvest interval, as calibration did in 0.1.1. (b) = thermal time accumulated by simulate_one_year() itself over the same interval, with planting forced to the observed date and the configured winter rules (vernalization 45 days at 0–10 °C, dormancy at ≤ 0 °C).
Crop Seasons (b)/(a) min p10 median mean p90 max Share < 0.99 Median (a) − (b), °C·day
Maize 279 1.000 1.000 1.000 1.000 1.000 1.000 0 0
Sugar beet 445 1.000 1.000 1.000 1.000 1.000 1.000 0 0
Winter wheat 323 0.685 0.773 0.844 0.842 0.902 0.930 100% 360.8

Per-station medians for winter wheat range from 0.742 to 0.884 (22 stations, tt_consistency_by_station.csv). One maize and one wheat season were excluded because the sowing year did not match the crop-year convention.

Reachability before the harvest deadline (simulation’s own planting rules, calibration years): with the 0.1.1 (raw) requirement, winter wheat could not accumulate the requirement by 15 August in 85.1% of 343 station-years; with a requirement calibrated by simulation rules, 23.9%. Maize 10.9% and sugar beet 3.9% under both.

Conclusion: the mismatch is confirmed for winter wheat only. For maize and sugar beet, calibration and simulation already agreed (up to floating-point rounding; see section 3).

Harvest deadline check (calibration years only, the 25 selected stations): 11.0% of 500 observed winter wheat harvests were after 15 August (median 4 Aug, p90 16 Aug, p95 20 Aug, latest 4 Sep). I did not judge this clearly inconsistent with German practice and left the deadline unchanged (open question 1).

2. The fix

  • New internal function accumulate_season_tt() (R/ThermoPheno_functions.R): the single implementation of daily thermal time + vernalization + dormancy + regrowth state, summed sequentially in double precision exactly as the 0.1.1 simulation loop did.
  • simulate_one_year() (and therefore run_simulation()) and estimate_required_tt() now call it instead of their own loops.
  • estimate_required_tt_from_observed() gains crop_type, winter_dormancy_temp, vernalization_required, vernalization_temp_min, vernalization_temp_max, vernalization_days_required, spring_regrowth_temp and accumulation = c("simulation", "raw"). The default is "simulation"; "raw" keeps the 0.1.1 sum. The returned list also has accumulation and crop_type. Help page, NEWS.md and the introduction article document it.
  • validation/dwd_validate_thermopheno.R: calibration and simulation now take the thermal-time rules from one list (tt_rules), and calibration uses accumulation = "simulation". Stations, years, filters, matching, minimum-data rules, metrics and crop_config.csv are unchanged. The column tt_calibration_method now reads observed_calendar/simulation.

Version 0.2.0, not 0.1.2: an exported function gets new arguments, and calibrating a winter crop with the new arguments gives substantially different values. Under pre-1.0 semantic versioning, that is a minor bump.

Default crop_type is "summer" (as in the other functions), so a 0.1.1-style call returns the same values as before (up to rounding). Users must pass crop_type = "winter" and the winter rules to get the corrected winter calibration. This keeps old calls stable but means a winter user who does not read the NEWS gets the old behaviour (open question 2).

3. Impact on earlier results

Cross-version comparison: validation/diagnostics/regression/ (each exported model function run with 0.1.1 and 0.2.0 on identical inputs: bundled historical weather and three DWD stations, 1991–2010, summer and winter defaults). Log: compare_v0.1.1_v0.2.0.log.

Exported function Changes vs 0.1.1? Example (old → new)
simulate_one_year(), run_simulation() No, for identical inputs (dates, statuses and accumulated TT identical) DWD 00150 winter: 20 seasons, 14 mature → identical
estimate_required_tt() winter No (bitwise identical) 1604.1228947368 → 1604.1228947368
estimate_required_tt() summer Floating-point only, ≤ 1.2e-12 °C·day 1267.8655250000 → 1267.8655250000
estimate_required_tt_from_observed(), 0.1.1-style call Floating-point only, ≤ 2.3e-12 °C·day; list has 2 extra elements 1272.3712500000 → 1272.3712500000
estimate_required_tt_from_observed() with crop_type = "winter" + rules New behaviour (not possible in 0.1.1) synthetic season 2048.82 → 1738.78; DWD wheat station medians ratio 0.779–0.876 (median 2378.7 → 1975.8)
prepare_weather(), calc_daily_tt(), find_planting_date(), default_parameters(), compare_validation_metrics(), validate_weather_dwd() Not modified –

Consequences for results produced earlier with ThermoPheno:

  • Winter-crop requirements from estimate_required_tt_from_observed() in 0.1.1 were raw sums (about 16% too high for the DWD wheat setup). Any winter-crop simulation driven by such a requirement tends to be late or forced at the harvest deadline. Such results should be recalibrated with crop_type = "winter" and the simulation’s winter rules.
  • Requirements from estimate_required_tt() (reference planting date + days to maturity) already applied the winter rules in 0.1.1 and are not affected. The Shiny app uses its own copy of this function (unchanged).
  • Summer crops: values differ only by ~1e-12 °C·day. Because daily TT from DWD temperatures lies on a 0.05 °C·day grid, exact ties between a simulated total and the requirement occur, and rounding can then move a maturity date by one day. This happened once in the DWD validation (maize, station 10353, 2019: 6 → 7 Sep, requirement 1099.275 → 1099.2750000000003).

4. Validation rerun

Script validation/dwd_validate_thermopheno.R with 0.2.0 installed. Outputs in pkgdown/assets/validation/; 0.1.1 outputs archived unchanged in pkgdown/assets/validation/archive/v0.1.1/. Comparison: validation/compare_validation_runs.R and validation/compare_common_cases.R (logs comparison_v0.1.1_vs_new.log, comparison_common_cases.log).

Inputs: all 48 DWD files have MD5 checksums identical to the 0.1.1 manifest. No DWD archive changed. Same 75 attempted cases, same station matches, same held-out station-years, identical simulated planting dates.

Maize: 8 forced, 0 failed in both. Sugar beet: 0 forced, 0 failed in both. Changed wheat harvests moved earlier by a median of 17 days (range 0 to −35).

Skill remains low for planting dates (R² ≤ 0.10) and sugar beet harvest. The article states this plainly, keeps the 75-case reporting, the exclusion table, the sugar beet 11908/2015 sensitivity note and the limitations, and adds “What changed in 0.2.0” and “Comparison with 0.1.1” sections.

Held-out data disclosure. The hypothesis came from the 0.1.1 held-out results (174 forced wheat harvests), which were already published. The confirmation, the fix and the tests used only 1991–2010 and synthetic data, and the deadline decision used only 1991–2010. I first saw 2011–2024 results for 0.2.0 after the package code and the validation configuration were final. After that I changed only reporting (comparison scripts, article, NEWS, this report), not code or configuration that affects results.

5. Tests

New: tests/testthat/test-tt-consistency.R and helper-synthetic-weather.R.

  • Round trip, winter and summer synthetic crops: calibrate from one season, simulate from the observed planting date, maturity within one day of the observed harvest (0.2.0: both exactly on the date).
  • Raw mode: accumulation = "raw" equals the value produced by 0.1.1 (2048.8223908266 winter, 1224.4860296517 summer) and the 0.1.1 formula, and fails the winter round trip (+19 days).
  • Equality: shared accumulator ≡ simulation accumulation (identical), ≡ an independent re-implementation of the 0.1.1 simulation loop, ≡ calibration over the same interval; baseline calibration ≡ reference loop.
  • Summer default ≡ raw up to 1e-12; winter simulation-rule calibration < raw.

Against 0.1.1: validation/diagnostics/roundtrip/roundtrip_v0.1.1.log shows the winter round trip failing (maturity 13 Aug vs observed 25 Jul, +19 days) and the summer one landing +1 day (rounding). new_tests_on_v0.1.1.log: the new test file fails 6 tests on 0.1.1 (the new arguments do not exist there). On 0.2.0 (roundtrip_v0.2.0.log) both round trips are exact. All tests pass on 0.2.0 (69 expectations, 0 failures).

On real data, validation/diagnostics/v0.2.0/diagnostic.log: calibration with accumulation = "simulation" equals the simulation’s accumulation for all 1,047 calibration seasons (maximum difference 0).

8. Open questions for the author

  1. Winter wheat harvest deadline (15 Aug). 11% of calibration-period harvests at the selected stations were later. 22 held-out harvests are still forced. I did not change it, and since I have now seen 2011–2024 results, any change should rest on a documented agronomic source chosen independently of them.
  2. Default crop_type = "summer" in estimate_required_tt_from_observed(). It keeps old calls stable, but a winter user who omits crop_type gets the raw-equivalent sum. Alternatives: warn when the call looks like a winter crop, or require crop_type (breaking).
  3. Maturity ties. The 0.05 °C·day grid makes exact ties common, so maturity on tie days depends on rounding. A small tolerance (e.g. cum >= req - 1e-9) would make it robust but changes simulation output in rare cases.
  4. Shiny app (inst/app/app.R) keeps its own copies of the model functions. It does not use observed calibration, so it is unaffected, but it is a second source of truth. Refactoring it to call the package functions is a separate task.
  5. Vernalization temperature window is not in crop_config.csv; the defaults (0–10 °C) are used on both sides. You may want it recorded explicitly.
  6. Branch. You decided to keep the changes on main without a separate branch or pull request. Review of the working-tree changes therefore stands in for PR approval before the v0.2.0 release. CI runs once the commit is pushed to main.
